question: Y133
answer:
THRESHOLD-EXCESS CALCULATION — ARTICLE 1(2)(a)–(b), COUNCIL REGULATION (EC) No 139/2004

Jurisdiction: European Union. Council Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 is directly applicable in all Member States and does not depend on national transposition. This memorandum is a draft for review by a qualified attorney. It is not legal advice.

====================================================================
1. QUESTION PRESENTED AND INSTRUCTION HONOURED
====================================================================
Question: by how much does each of three recorded turnover amounts — combined aggregate worldwide EUR 5,400 million; Community-wide EUR 300 million; Community-wide EUR 275 million — exceed the corresponding Article 1(2) turnover threshold, and is each threshold exceeded?

Instruction honoured: this memorandum does NOT decide whether the concentration has a Community dimension. It performs three subtractions and three strict-inequality comparisons, and stops there. See section 6 below for the matters expressly left open.

====================================================================
2. GOVERNING AUTHORITY
====================================================================
(1) Council Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 of 20 January 2004 on the control of concentrations between undertakings (the EC Merger Regulation), OJ L 24, 29.1.2004, p. 1–22; CELEX 32004R0139.
    — Article 1(2), opening words and points (a) and (b):
      'A concentration has a Community dimension where:
       (a) the combined aggregate worldwide turnover of all the undertakings concerned is more than EUR 5 000 million; and
       (b) the aggregate Community-wide turnover of each of at least two of the undertakings concerned is more than EUR 250 million,
       unless each of the undertakings concerned achieves more than two-thirds of its aggregate Community-wide turnover within one and the same Member State.'
      (The OJ text prints the figures with a thin space as thousands separator: 'EUR 5 000 million' and 'EUR 250 million'. These are the same figures as EUR 5,000 million and EUR 250 million used in this memorandum.)
    — Article 1(3): alternative thresholds (context only; not applied here — see section 6).
    — Article 5: calculation of turnover (paragraph 1, definition of turnover and the 'preceding financial year' reference year; paragraph 2, acquisitions of parts of undertakings; paragraph 4, aggregation across the group and elimination of turnover between the undertakings concerned to avoid double counting; paragraph 5, credit and financial institutions). Not applied here — see section 7.
    — Recital 9: the Regulation's scope is defined by quantitative thresholds, so that concentrations which by reason of their size are liable to have a significant impact are caught and those which are not are not notified. (Recital numbering to be confirmed against the OJ text before citation in a filed document — see section 7(d).)

(2) Commission Consolidated Jurisdictional Notice under Council Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 on the control of concentrations between undertakings, OJ C 95, 16.4.2008, p. 1–48. Relevant for its treatment of the calculation of turnover and of the two-thirds-of-Community-wide-turnover rule. Non-binding interpretive guidance; it does not alter the Article 1(2) figures.

(3) No amending instrument altering the Article 1(2) EUR figures is relied on. See section 7(a).

====================================================================
3. THE THREE COMPARISONS — RESULT
====================================================================
All amounts in EUR million. Threshold figures are those of Article 1(2) of Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 as cited in section 2(1).

 #  Recorded amount                                   Provision        Threshold     Excess        Threshold exceeded?
--- -------------------------------------------------- ---------------- ------------- ------------- ---------------------
 1  Combined aggregate worldwide turnover: 5,400       Art. 1(2)(a)     5,000         400           Yes (5,400 > 5,000)
 2  Aggregate Community-wide turnover, undertaking A:  Art. 1(2)(b)     250           50            Yes (300 > 250)
    300
 3  Aggregate Community-wide turnover, undertaking B:  Art. 1(2)(b)     250           25            Yes (275 > 250)
    275

Arithmetic, written out:
  (1) 5,400 − 5,000 = 400  → excess of EUR 400 million over the worldwide threshold.
  (2)   300 −   250 =  50  → excess of EUR 50 million over the Community-wide threshold.
  (3)   275 −   250 =  25  → excess of EUR 25 million over the Community-wide threshold.

====================================================================
4. WHY THE TWO COMMUNITY-WIDE FIGURES ARE TWO COMPARISONS, NOT ONE
====================================================================
Article 1(2)(b) is framed per undertaking: 'the aggregate Community-wide turnover of each of at least two of the undertakings concerned is more than EUR 250 million'. The unit of comparison is therefore each undertaking concerned, measured against a single figure of EUR 250 million. On the figures supplied, EUR 300 million and EUR 275 million are each compared separately with EUR 250 million, producing two distinct excesses (EUR 50 million and EUR 25 million). They are not added together and are not compared as a combined EUR 575 million against any threshold; the Regulation contains no combined Community-wide threshold in Article 1(2)(b).

Consequence in strict arithmetic terms only: the 'at least two of the undertakings concerned' limb of Article 1(2)(b) is numerically satisfied on these figures, because two undertakings each record more than EUR 250 million of Community-wide turnover. Whether that limb is ultimately satisfied in law is a different question (section 6).

====================================================================
5. STATUS OF THE TWO-THIRDS RULE IN THIS CALCULATION
====================================================================
The words following Article 1(2)(b) ('unless each of the undertakings concerned achieves more than two-thirds of its aggregate Community-wide turnover within one and the same Member State') are a disapplication condition, not a threshold. They do not change the EUR 250 million figure, they do not change the subtraction, and they therefore do not change any of the three excess amounts reported in section 3. They operate only after the numerical thresholds are found to be met, and only on geographic-distribution data (per-undertaking turnover by Member State) which is not part of the recorded figures supplied. No view is expressed on whether the condition is met. See section 6.

====================================================================
6. MATTERS EXPRESSLY NOT DECIDED (COMPLIANCE WITH THE INSTRUCTION)
====================================================================
Pursuant to the instruction, this memorandum does not decide, and expresses no view on, any of the following:
  (a) whether the concentration has a Community dimension;
  (b) whether the cumulative Article 1(2) test is satisfied — Article 1(2)(a) and (b) are cumulative ('and'), so the fact that all three recorded amounts individually exceed their thresholds is a necessary but not a sufficient condition, and I make no finding on sufficiency;
  (c) whether the two-thirds-of-one-and-the-same-Member-State disapplication applies to either or both undertakings, which turns on the geographic breakdown of each undertaking's Community-wide turnover and cannot be assessed on the figures supplied;
  (d) whether the Article 1(3) alternative thresholds are met, or whether any referral under Article 4(5) or Article 22 is available or appropriate — these are noted as context only and are outside the scope of the question asked;
  (e) whether the concentration is a 'concentration' within Article 3, or which entities are the 'undertakings concerned' within Article 5(4).

====================================================================
7. WHERE THE AUTHORITY IS THIN, UNVERIFIED, OR DEPENDENT ON FACTS NOT SUPPLIED
====================================================================
(a) VERSION OF THE THRESHOLDS — the principal open point. The calculation in section 3 applies the Article 1(2) figures as adopted in Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 (EUR 5,000 million; EUR 250 million). I was unable to verify, from the sources retrieved, any amending instrument that has altered those two EUR figures, and in particular I could not verify the reference in the instructing brief to 'Commission Regulation (EU) No 2022/1681' as an act amending the Article 1(2) thresholds. That reference is therefore not relied on and is not cited as authority. Before this calculation is used in a filing, counsel should confirm the position as at the applicable filing/assessment date against EUR-Lex (CELEX 32004R0139, 'All consolidated versions') and against the Commission's merger legislation page. If an amending act with a different EUR figure does govern the filing date, the three subtractions in section 3 must be re-run against the amended figures; the method is unchanged, only the subtrahends move. This is the one point on which the numbers in section 3 are conditional.
(b) ARTICLE 5 ADJUSTMENTS. The calculation takes the amounts 'as recorded', as instructed. It does not apply Article 5: in particular it does not verify that the worldwide figure is the sum of the group turnovers required by Article 5(4), that sales between the undertakings concerned have been eliminated to avoid double counting, that the correct 'preceding financial year' has been used, or that the Community-wide figure is turnover 'within the Community' in the Article 5 sense (including the treatment of exports). If any Article 5 adjustment is required, the recorded amounts — and therefore the excesses — would change. The excesses in section 3 are excesses of the recorded amounts, not of Article 5-compliant turnover.
(c) CURRENCY AND ROUNDING. All amounts are assumed to be stated in euro and already converted where the underlying turnover arose in another currency; no conversion or rounding adjustment is made. If conversion is required, the applicable exchange-rate convention should be taken from the notification form (Form CO) in the implementing regulation and pinned to its OJ text before reliance.
(d) PINNING OF SECONDARY REFERENCES. The recital number given in section 2(1) and the paragraph numbers of the Consolidated Jurisdictional Notice referred to in section 2(2) should be verified against the OJ texts before they are quoted in a filed document. They are offered as pointers, not as verified pinpoint citations. The operative legal statements in sections 3 to 6 rest on the Article 1(2) text itself, not on the recitals or the Notice.
(e) NO CONFLICT OF AUTHORITY IDENTIFIED. On the narrow arithmetical question asked, the position is straightforward and I found no conflicting authority: Article 1(2)(a) sets one figure and Article 1(2)(b) sets one figure, and the comparison is strict ('more than'). The thinness lies in the version point at (a) and the factual inputs at (b), not in any divergence between sources.

====================================================================
8. ONE-LINE ANSWER FOR THE FILE
====================================================================
Against the Article 1(2) thresholds of Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 (EUR 5,000 million worldwide; EUR 250 million Community-wide), the recorded amounts exceed their thresholds by EUR 400 million (worldwide), EUR 50 million (Community-wide, undertaking A) and EUR 25 million (Community-wide, undertaking B); all three thresholds are exceeded on the recorded figures. No conclusion is drawn on Community dimension.

====================================================================
9. VERIFICATION NOTE
====================================================================
Internal consistency check performed: the three excesses (400 / 50 / 25) are differences only and are never used as thresholds; each is strictly smaller than the recorded amount from which it is derived; each threshold appears with a single figure throughout (5,000 / 250 / 250); and no computed value in this memorandum is stated as exceeding a limit that this memorandum itself sets. The strict-inequality direction ('more than') is preserved in every comparison: 5,400 > 5,000; 300 > 250; 275 > 250.
cautions: The recompute vote compared nothing, so no figure in this answer was recomputed independently.
A lookup ran, but no page it named could be read, so nothing in this answer was checked against a source.

question: Y134
answer:
MEMORANDUM — DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED ATTORNEY. NOT LEGAL ADVICE.

Subject: Directive 2011/83/EU, Article 3(4) low-value off-premises exclusion — whether two simultaneous related-subject contracts (EUR 30 + EUR 25) are aggregated for the EUR 50 threshold, and whether the exclusion covers the pair.

JURISDICTION. The addressee is an EU Member State that has exercised the Article 3(4) option at the EUR 50 maximum. The Member State is not identified in the instruction. Part A states the Union-law position, which is the same in every Member State that has taken the option at EUR 50; Part E lists the national-law variables that must be checked before the conclusion is applied to a specific file. The Directive is Directive 2011/83/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 October 2011 on consumer rights, OJ L 304, 22.11.2011, p. 64–88, as amended (most recently for these purposes by Directive (EU) 2015/2302, OJ L 326, 11.12.2015, p. 1).

A. QUESTIONS PRESENTED AND SHORT ANSWERS

A.1 Question 1 (value). Where a consumer simultaneously concludes two off-premises contracts with related subjects requiring payments of EUR 30 and EUR 25, what total is used to apply the Article 3(4) EUR 50 threshold?

Answer: EUR 55. The two payments are aggregated. The threshold is applied to the total cost of the related contracts, not to each contract separately.

A.2 Question 2 (verdict). Does the optional exclusion, taken at the EUR 50 maximum, cover this pair on that basis?

Answer: No. EUR 55 exceeds EUR 50. Article 3(4) is available only where the payment 'does not exceed EUR 50'. The pair is outside the exclusion; Directive 2011/83/EU applies in full to both contracts.

B. AUTHORITIES RELIED ON

B.1 Directive 2011/83/EU, Article 3(4) (operative provision, verbatim): 'Member States may decide not to apply this Directive or not to maintain or introduce corresponding national provisions to off-premises contracts for which the payment to be made by the consumer does not exceed EUR 50. Member States may define a lower value in their national legislation.'

B.2 Directive 2011/83/EU, Recital 28 (verbatim, in relevant part): 'In order to avoid administrative burden being placed on traders, Member States may decide not to apply this Directive where goods or services of a minor value are sold off-premises. The monetary threshold should be established at a sufficiently low level as to exclude only purchases of small significance. Member States should be allowed to define this value in their national legislation provided that it does not exceed EUR 50. Where two or more contracts with related subjects are concluded at the same time by the consumer, the total cost thereof should be taken into account for the purpose of applying this threshold.'

B.3 Directive 2011/83/EU, Article 2(8) (definition of 'off-premises contract') and Article 2(9) (definition of 'business premises') — relevant to confirming that both contracts are off-premises contracts in the first place; the exclusion in Article 3(4) operates only on contracts that are off-premises within Article 2(8).

B.4 European Commission, Guidance on the interpretation and application of Directive 2011/83/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on consumer rights, OJ C 525, 29.12.2021, p. 1, section 1.8 ('Possible exemption of low value off-premises contracts'). The Guidance states that Article 3(4) creates a circumvention risk where traders 'artificially split a single contract above the set threshold into several contracts', invokes Recital 28, and gives as examples 'selling each book of a trilogy under three separate contracts or selling a pair of earrings under two separate contracts at the same time'. It adds that for long-term contracts (subscriptions) the relevant amount is the total amount the consumer commits to pay over the agreed contractual period, including 'free' periods. Status: administrative guidance, not binding on the Court of Justice or on national courts. Pin-cite and OJ reference to be re-verified against the published text before filing.

B.5 Court of Justice, Case C-162/97 Nilsson and Others [1998] ECR I-7477, para. 54 — the preamble of a Union act has no binding legal force and cannot be relied on to derogate from the operative provisions. Cited for the correct weight to give Recital 28: it interprets Article 3(4), it does not override it.

B.6 Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Article 288, third paragraph — a directive binds Member States as to the result to be achieved; the Article 3(4) option exists only in national law once exercised.

C. ANALYSIS

C.1 Article 3(4) is a Member State option, not a self-executing rule. Its wording ('may decide not to apply') means that the exclusion exists for a given consumer only if, and to the extent that, the Member State has transposed it. The ceiling is EUR 50; a Member State may set a lower figure. The instruction states that the Member State has taken the option at the maximum, so the applicable threshold is EUR 50.

C.2 Article 3(4) is silent on how to treat related contracts concluded together. Recital 28 fills that gap: 'Where two or more contracts with related subjects are concluded at the same time by the consumer, the total cost thereof should be taken into account for the purpose of applying this threshold.' Two cumulative conditions: (i) two or more contracts; (ii) related subjects, concluded at the same time.

C.3 Both conditions are satisfied on the facts put to me. The instruction states that the consumer 'simultaneously concludes two contracts with related subjects'. That is the paradigm case the Commission Guidance identifies (trilogy sold as three contracts; a pair of earrings sold as two). No further characterisation is needed to answer the question as posed.

C.4 Application — worked threshold test:

  Contract 1 payment ................ EUR 30
  Contract 2 payment ................ EUR 25
  Aggregated total (30 + 25) ........ EUR 55
  Applicable threshold (maximum) .... EUR 50
  Statutory test .................... total 'does not exceed EUR 50' (total <= 50)
  Comparison ........................ EUR 55 > EUR 50 (exceeds by EUR 5)
  Result ............................ test failed; exclusion unavailable

C.5 Consequence. Because the exclusion is unavailable, both contracts remain off-premises contracts within Article 2(8) and the Directive applies to each of them. In practice, for each contract the trader owes: the pre-contractual information listed in Article 6(1) (including, at point (h), the existence and conditions of the right of withdrawal); the formal confirmation requirements of Article 7 (including the model withdrawal form and the confirmation on paper or, if the consumer agrees, another durable medium); and the consumer has the 14-day right of withdrawal under Article 9(1), running as provided in Article 9(2). If the withdrawal information is not given, the period is extended under Article 10(1) by up to 12 months, and Article 10(2) applies if the information is supplied late. Article 15 governs the effect of withdrawal on any ancillary contract between the same trader and consumer. Article 25 makes the consumer's rights non-waivable, and Article 24 requires effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties for infringement.

C.6 The trader's contrary argument, and its answer. The trader will say: Article 3(4) speaks of 'the payment to be made by the consumer' in the singular and asks whether it 'does not exceed EUR 50'; each contract here is EUR 30 and EUR 25 respectively, each below EUR 50, so each is excluded. The answer is that Recital 28 expressly addresses that reading and forecloses it where the two contracts have related subjects and are concluded at the same time; the recital exists precisely because a per-contract reading would let a trader split a EUR 55 transaction into two EUR 30/EUR 25 contracts and defeat the threshold. Recital 28 does not contradict Article 3(4) — it supplies the method of measuring 'the payment' in the multi-contract case — so the Nilsson principle (B.5) is not an obstacle. A reading of Article 3(4) that permitted the split would also frustrate the effectiveness (effet utile) of the consumer-protection rules the threshold is meant only to disapply for purchases 'of small significance' (Recital 28).

C.7 Where the authority is thin, stated plainly. (a) Recital 28 is the only Union-law text containing the aggregation rule; Article 3(4) does not contain it. Its force is interpretative, not operative, and a national court asked to apply a purely literal national transposition could in principle reach a different result. (b) I have not located a Court of Justice judgment construing the aggregation sentence of Recital 28; the only Union-level application I can point to is the non-binding Commission Guidance at B.4. A targeted search of national case law on contract-splitting in the relevant Member State is required before relying on the conclusion in litigation. (c) The Directive does not define 'related subjects'. It is an autonomous Union concept to be construed uniformly, but its outer boundary (for example, two genuinely independent purchases made in the same visit) is undecided at Union level and is a factual assessment for the national court.

D. SENSITIVITY — WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER

D.1 If the Member State set a threshold lower than EUR 50, the pair remains outside the exclusion a fortiori (EUR 55 exceeds any lower figure).

D.2 If the Member State never exercised the Article 3(4) option, the question is moot: the Directive applies regardless of value, and the trader cannot rely on an option the Member State did not take (Article 3(4); TFEU Article 288).

D.3 If the two contracts did not have 'related subjects' — genuinely independent purchases in the same visit — Recital 28 would not aggregate them, each would be tested separately (EUR 30 <= 50; EUR 25 <= 50), and both would fall within the exclusion if the national provision so provides. This is the single factual pivot on which the verdict turns, and it is stipulated in the instruction, not assumed by me.

D.4 VAT basis. Neither Article 3(4) nor Recital 28 states whether the EUR 50 is computed gross or net of VAT, and the Commission Guidance does not resolve it. The instruction supplies the payments actually to be made (EUR 30 and EUR 25) and the project assumptions treat them as nominal consumer-facing values. On a like-for-like comparison the total is EUR 55 and exceeds EUR 50. If, however, the national provision applied the threshold net of VAT while the stated amounts were gross, a standard-rate figure of EUR 55 gross would be EUR 45.83 net and would fall below EUR 50, reversing the result. This must be checked against the national text and, if relevant, the national VAT rate. It is flagged, not assumed away.

E. CONDITIONS AND VERIFICATION CHECKLIST BEFORE THE CONCLUSION IS APPLIED TO A FILE

E.1 Identify the Member State and cite its transposing provision verbatim (statute, article, paragraph).
E.2 Confirm the national threshold is EUR 50 and not lower, and confirm the VAT basis on which the national provision measures 'payment'.
E.3 Confirm whether the national provision contains an express aggregation clause for simultaneous related contracts, or whether aggregation would rest on conforming interpretation of Recital 28; if the latter, record the national interpretive canon (e.g. directive-conforming interpretation of national law) and any contrary national authority.
E.4 Record the facts establishing 'related subjects' and 'concluded at the same time': same trader, same visit, same commercial purpose, split invoicing, single delivery, cross-referencing contract numbers.
E.5 Check for national anti-circumvention or abuse-of-splitting rules that may operate independently of Article 3(4).
E.6 If the exclusion is found inapplicable, audit compliance with Articles 6, 7, 9, 10 and 15 for each contract, and quantify exposure under the national penalty provision implementing Article 24.

F. BOTTOM LINE FOR THE FILE

Total for the threshold: EUR 55 (aggregated under Recital 28 because the two contracts have related subjects and were concluded at the same time). Threshold: EUR 50. EUR 55 exceeds EUR 50. The optional exclusion does not cover this pair; both off-premises contracts carry the full information and withdrawal regime of Directive 2011/83/EU, subject to the national-law verification in Part E.
cautions: The answer gives 55 EUR for ask 1, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.

question: Y135
answer:
MEMORANDUM — RESEARCH DRAFT FOR ATTORNEY REVIEW
Not legal advice. Every statement of law below is tied to a cited source; items needing verification before filing are flagged in Part VII.

====================================================================
I. QUESTIONS PRESENTED
====================================================================
1. (Constraint.) The governing text is the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure as amended to December 1, 2025. Jurisdiction: United States district courts (federal). No state procedural analog is considered or imported; a state's forms appendix is governed by that state's rules and is outside this memorandum.
2. In that text, what is the current status of the "Appendix of Forms" to which a 2014 litigation manual still directs users?
3. When did that change take effect?

====================================================================
II. SHORT ANSWERS
====================================================================
2. STATUS — ABROGATED. The Appendix of Forms no longer exists as operative rule text. Title XII of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure now carries only an abrogation note: "APPENDIX OF FORMS [Abrogated (Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015).]" The implementing rule, former Rule 84, likewise reads: "Rule 84. [Abrogated (Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015).]" There is no successor official forms appendix in the FRCP; the forms were not relocated elsewhere in the rules.

3. EFFECTIVE DATE — DECEMBER 1, 2015. The Supreme Court adopted the amendment by order dated April 29, 2015, and specified December 1, 2015, as the effective date. April 29, 2015 is the adoption/transmittal date; December 1, 2015 is the date the change took effect. Both dates appear in the citation itself: "(Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015)."

Consequence for the 2014 manual: its direction to the Appendix of Forms has been obsolete since December 1, 2015 — more than ten years as of the December 1, 2025 text. The manual's statement is not merely dated; it points to text that no longer exists.

====================================================================
III. AUTHORITIES RELIED ON (FULL CITATIONS)
====================================================================
Primary — the rule text as amended to December 1, 2025:
 A. Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 84 and Title XII (Appendix of Forms), as amended to December 1, 2025, reproduced at Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School, https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frcp (index page stating "These are the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, as amended to December 1, 2025," and listing "Rule 84. Abrogated, eff. Dec. 1, 2015" and "XII. APPENDIX OF FORMS [Abrogated (Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015)].").
 B. Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, as amended to December 1, 2024 (U.S. Courts, official judiciary website), https://www.uscourts.gov/file/document/federal-rules-civil-procedure-1 — Rule 84 and the Appendix of Forms each appear as "[Abrogated (Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015).]" Used as a cross-check on the 2025 text.
 C. Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, as amended to December 1, 2015 (U.S. Courts), https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/frcp.12.1.2015_1.pdf — same abrogation notes, confirming the change was already reflected in the first text published after the effective date.

Primary — the amending instrument:
 D. Order of the Supreme Court of the United States, dated April 29, 2015, amending the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (Rules 1, 4, 16, 26, 30, 31, 33, 34, 37, 55, and 84, and the Appendix of Forms), effective December 1, 2015, transmitted to Congress pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 2072, https://www.supremecourt.gov/orders/courtorders/frcv15(update)_1823.pdf. Operative language: "1. That the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure be, and they hereby are, amended by including therein amendments to Civil Rules 1, 4, 16, 26, 30, 31, 33, 34, 37, 55, and 84, and the Appendix of Forms. ... 2. That the foregoing amendments to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure shall take effect on December 1, 2015, and shall govern in all proceedings in civil cases thereafter commenced and, insofar as just and practicable, all proceedings then pending. 3. That THE CHIEF JUSTICE be, and hereby is, authorized to transmit to the Congress the foregoing amendments ... in accordance with the provisions of Section 2072 of Title 28, United States Code." The same order prints the amended rules with the notes "Rule 84. Forms [Abrogated (Apr. __, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015).]" and "APPENDIX OF FORMS [Abrogated (Apr. __, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015).]"

Primary — statutory framework:
 E. 28 U.S.C. § 2072 (Rules Enabling Act) — the statutory authority under which the Supreme Court promulgates and transmits the civil rules to Congress (cited in paragraph 3 of the April 29, 2015 order).
 F. 28 U.S.C. § 2074 — governs the effective date of rules promulgated under the Act; cross-referenced by Fed. R. Civ. P. 86(a) ("These rules and any amendments take effect at the time specified by the Supreme Court, subject to 28 U.S.C. § 2074.").
 G. Fed. R. Civ. P. 86(a) (Effective Dates) — quoted above from the current text.

Official judiciary confirmation (secondary, but authoritative within the judiciary):
 H. Federal Judicial Center, "Amendments to the Federal Rules of Practice and Procedure 2015—Civil Rules Redline" (Dec. 1, 2015), https://www.fjc.gov/content/309299/amendments-federal-rules-practice-and-procedure-2015-civil-rules-redline — "Amendments to the following Federal Rules of Civil Procedure became effective on December 1, 2015: 1, 4, 16, 26, 30, 31, 33, 34, 37, and 55. Rule 84 and the Appendix of Forms were abrogated."
 I. Federal Judicial Center, "Amendments to the Federal Rules of Practice and Procedure 2015—Transmittal to Congress" (April 29, 2015), https://www.fjc.gov/federal-rules-practice-and-procedure/fed.-r.-civil-p.-31 — records that the package "was transmitted to Congress on April 29, 2015 ... to become effective on December 1, 2015."

Pleading-standard authority relevant to Part V (unchanged by the abrogation):
 J. Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544 (2007).
 K. Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662 (2009).
 L. Fed. R. Civ. P. 8(a)(2) (short and plain statement of the claim); Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6) (failure to state a claim).

====================================================================
IV. ANALYSIS
====================================================================
A. The appendix's status in the text as amended to December 1, 2025.

1. The current text contains no forms. In the rules as amended to December 1, 2025, Title XII consists of a single bracketed line: "APPENDIX OF FORMS [Abrogated (Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015).]" Authority C (the December 1, 2015 print) and Authority B (the December 1, 2024 print) show the identical line, so the 2025 text reflects no intervening reinstatement. Authority A (the December 1, 2025 text) lists Title XII in the same form. Nothing was added in place of the abrogated forms.

2. The gateway rule was abrogated too. Former Rule 84 was the provision that gave the appendix its operative effect — it told readers that the forms in the appendix sufficed under the rules. In the current text Rule 84 reads only: "Rule 84. [Abrogated (Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015).]" (Authorities A, B, C.) Because both the gateway rule and the appendix are gone, a direction to "the Appendix of Forms" now points to a heading that exists only as a tombstone.

3. "Abrogated" means repealed, not revised. The distinction matters because the request asks for "status," which could mean either (i) formal repeal or (ii) content revision. The answer here is (i): formal repeal. The April 29, 2015 order lists "Rule 84, and the Appendix of Forms" among the provisions "amended," and the resulting text uses the standard abrogation formulation with no replacement content (Authority D). The FJC states the point in terms: "Rule 84 and the Appendix of Forms were abrogated" (Authority H). No form in the former appendix survives as official rule text.

4. What was NOT abrogated. The Supplemental Rules for Admiralty or Maritime Claims and Asset Forfeiture Actions (Title XIII, Rules A–G) remain in force and are a separate body of rules, not an "appendix of forms"; they follow the abrogated Title XII in the current text (Authorities A, B, C). Individual rules also continue to prescribe the content or form of particular papers — e.g., Rule 4(a)(1) (contents of the summons), Rule 58(b) (separate judgment), Rule 65(d) (form and scope of injunctions) — and those requirements are unaffected. Local forms adopted under Fed. R. Civ. P. 83 and forms published on court websites are separate sources and are unaffected by the abrogation of the national appendix.

B. The effective date, and what it is not.

1. The date. December 1, 2015. The Supreme Court's April 29, 2015 order states in terms that the amendments "shall take effect on December 1, 2015" (Authority D, paragraph 2). The rule text records the same date in the standard parenthetical: "(Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015)" (Authorities A, B, C). The FJC confirms that the amendments "became effective on December 1, 2015" and that "Rule 84 and the Appendix of Forms were abrogated" as part of that package (Authority H).

2. The mechanics, for the file. The Court promulgated and transmitted the amendments to Congress on April 29, 2015, under 28 U.S.C. § 2072 (Authority D, paragraph 3; Authority I). Under Fed. R. Civ. P. 86(a), the rules "take effect at the time specified by the Supreme Court, subject to 28 U.S.C. § 2074" (Authority G). The specified time was December 1, 2015. The order further provides that the amendments govern "all proceedings in civil cases thereafter commenced and, insofar as just and practicable, all proceedings then pending" (Authority D, paragraph 2) — the standard temporal reach provision, relevant if a pending case is at issue.

3. Three dates that must not be confused:
 - April 29, 2015 — adoption and transmittal to Congress. NOT the effective date.
 - December 1, 2015 — effective date. This is the answer to ask 3.
 - December 1, 2025 — the currency date of the text consulted (ask 1's constraint). Not a change date for the appendix; no amendment to Rule 84 or Title XII appears between 2015 and 2025 in the current text (Authority A).

4. Correcting a common assumption. The 2015 package did restyle a number of civil rules, but the Rule 84/Appendix change was substantive abrogation, not restyling, and it was not part of the 2007 restyling that renumbered and restyled the rules generally. A manual dated 2014 post-dates the 2007 restyling and pre-dates the 2015 abrogation, which is exactly why its direction to the appendix was accurate when written and is wrong now.

C. Which "appendix" the manual means — disambiguation.

Because the answer differs by referent, the following table states the position for each candidate reading. This memorandum assumes reading (1), the standard referent of the unqualified phrase.

 (1) FRCP Appendix of Forms (former Title XII, implementing former Rule 84): ABROGATED, eff. Dec. 1, 2015. This is the answer above.
 (2) Supplemental Rules for Admiralty or Maritime Claims and Asset Forfeiture Actions (Title XIII): IN FORCE, unaffected. Not a forms appendix.
 (3) Forms or content requirements embedded in individual rules (Rules 4, 45, 58, 65, etc.): IN FORCE, unaffected.
 (4) Local court forms under Fed. R. Civ. P. 83: unaffected; validity depends on the individual district's local rules.
 (5) Forms appendices to other rule sets (Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure, Bankruptcy Official Forms, Appellate Rules): outside the FRCP; not addressed here.

If the manual's direction cannot be tied to reading (1), the analysis must be redone against the specific appendix it names. The wording of the manual's direction should be checked before the memorandum is finalized.

D. What this means for the 2014 manual's guidance.

1. The guidance is stale on this point. A direction to "see the Appendix of Forms" cannot be followed in the current rules: the appendix is abrogated and no form in it survives as official text. The manual should be corrected, and any brief, checklist, or training material that repeats the direction should be corrected with it.

2. The abrogation did not invalidate pleadings or papers that were drafted with the former forms in mind. What changed is the safe harbor: former Rule 84 told readers that the appendix forms sufficed under the rules, and that assurance no longer exists in the text. Sufficiency of a pleading is now tested solely against the rules themselves — principally Rule 8(a)(2) and Rule 12(b)(6) as construed in Twombly and Iqbal (Authorities J, K, L). A paper modeled on an old form is not defective for that reason, but it earns no deference for that reason either.

3. Practical direction for the drafter: cite the rule, not the form. Where the 2014 manual said "use Form __," substitute the operative rule (e.g., Rule 8 for the pleading, Rule 12 for the responsive pleading, Rule 4(a)(1) for the summons content, Rule 58 for the judgment). Where a court's own website or local rules supply a required form, cite that source instead.

====================================================================
V. WHERE AUTHORITY IS THIN OR CONFLICTING — STATED PLAINLY
====================================================================
1. No conflict in the primary sources. The Supreme Court order (Authority D), the current rule text (Authorities A, B, C), and the FJC's official description (Authority H) are consistent: abrogation, effective December 1, 2015. There is no split or ambiguity to resolve on the two questions asked.

2. Thin authority on collateral effect. No Supreme Court or court of appeals decision construing the effect of the Rule 84 abrogation on the sufficiency of any particular pleading was identified in this research, and none is cited here. The conclusion in Part IV.D.2 rests on the text of the rules (Rule 8(a)(2), Rule 12(b)(6)) and on Twombly/Iqbal, not on a decision about the abrogation. Do not represent to a court that case law holds that former forms retain any status; the supportable statement is the narrower one: the forms are no longer part of the rules and carry no safe-harbor effect.

3. Verification still owed before filing (see Part VII). The two points below are the only ones on which this draft relies on recollection rather than on a source in hand, and both are flagged at the point of use rather than asserted as verified.

====================================================================
VI. HOW TO STATE IT IN A FILING (suggested language)
====================================================================
"The Appendix of Forms to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure was abrogated, together with Rule 84, by amendments adopted by the Supreme Court on April 29, 2015, and effective December 1, 2015. See Order of April 29, 2015, amending the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, eff. Dec. 1, 2015; Fed. R. Civ. P. 84 (abrogated Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015); Fed. R. Civ. P., tit. XII (Appendix of Forms) (abrogated Apr. 29, 2015, eff. Dec. 1, 2015). There is no longer an official forms appendix to the civil rules."

====================================================================
VII. VERIFICATION CHECKLIST BEFORE THE MEMORANDUM IS FINALIZED
====================================================================
1. Quote the pre-abrogation text of former Rule 84 from an official pre-2015 edition (the "forms in the Appendix suffice" language) rather than from recollection; the paraphrase in Part IV.A.2 is safe as written, but any direct quotation must be checked against the 2014 print.
2. Quote the Judicial Conference Committee Note to the 2015 abrogation of Rule 84 from the official transmittal package (Authority I) if the memorandum is to explain the rulemakers' stated rationale. This draft deliberately does not quote that Note.
3. Replace the Legal Information Institute citation (Authority A) with the official U.S. Government Publishing Office / House Judiciary Committee print of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure as amended to December 1, 2025, for any filing or client-facing use. LII is a reliable reproduction but is not the official text; the uscourts.gov copy available for this research was current only to December 1, 2024 (Authority B), though it agrees on the point at issue.
4. Confirm the exact wording of the 2014 manual's direction, so that Part IV.C's assumption (reading (1)) can be verified rather than assumed.
5. If a specific case is pending, confirm the temporal-reach language of the April 29, 2015 order (Authority D, paragraph 2) applies as the order states.

====================================================================
VIII. BOTTOM LINE
====================================================================
- Ask 2: the Appendix of Forms is ABROGATED in the rules as amended to December 1, 2025; Title XII survives only as an abrogation note, and former Rule 84 is abrogated with it.
- Ask 3: the change took effect DECEMBER 1, 2015 (adopted April 29, 2015).
- The 2014 manual's direction to the appendix has been obsolete for over a decade and should be replaced with citations to the operative rules or to the individual court's local forms.

This is a research draft for review by a qualified attorney. It is not legal advice, and no attorney-client relationship is created.
